Amanda's face is widely circulated by the news, but the circumstances of her home life and disappearance make it difficult to know whether she was taken by a stranger or by someone connected to her family.
characters.name: Amanda McCready

characters.description: Amanda's mother, whose neglect is central to the circumstances of the disappearance. Helene left her young daughter alone while she went to a bar and responds to attention with a mixture of defensiveness, self-interest, and flashes of concern. Her connections in the neighborhood complicate the search.
characters.name: Helene McCready

characters.description: Helene's brother and Amanda's uncle, who approaches Patrick and Angie with his wife to ask for help finding the child. Lionel presents himself as the steadier member of a troubled family and believes local investigators may reach people who will not cooperate with police.
characters.name: Lionel McCready

characters.description: Lionel's wife and Amanda's aunt. Beatrice is openly appalled by Helene's parenting and is a driving force behind hiring Patrick and Angie. Her fear for Amanda is accompanied by anger that the child was left vulnerable in the first place.
characters.name: Beatrice McCready

characters.description: A veteran police captain associated with the official search for Amanda. Doyle's own child was abducted and murdered years earlier, giving him a personal understanding of the case and a reputation shaped by the protection of children.
characters.name: Captain Jack Doyle

characters.description: A police detective assigned to Amanda's disappearance. Remy is an experienced, forceful investigator who knows the city's violent offenders and works with Patrick and Angie despite the tension between official police procedure and their neighborhood methods.
characters.name: Remy Broussard

characters.description: Remy Broussard's police partner in the investigation of Amanda's disappearance. Poole is part of the uneasy cooperation between the detectives and the private investigators as they pursue leads through Dorchester's criminal circles.
characters.name: Nick Poole

characters.description: Patrick's dangerous but fiercely loyal friend, an arms dealer whose resources and capacity for violence make him useful when an investigation moves beyond what ordinary police channels can handle. Bubba's loyalty is chiefly to Patrick and Angie rather than to rules or institutions.
characters.name: Bubba Rogowski

characters.description: A powerful drug dealer connected to money stolen by Helene and one of her associates. Cheese's criminal organization and threats provide a plausible motive for taking Amanda, forcing the investigators to negotiate in a world where a child's safety can be treated as leverage.
characters.name: Cheese Olamon

recaps.ending: Patrick and Angie discover that Amanda did not die during the failed exchange. Her abduction was redirected into a plan involving members of the investigation and her uncle Lionel, with retired captain Jack Doyle ultimately keeping her in a safe, attentive home. Doyle argues that Amanda's welfare matters more than Helene's legal claim, and Angie agrees that returning the child would condemn her to neglect. Patrick believes that allowing a kidnapping to stand would make him responsible for deciding who deserves another person's child. He alerts the authorities. Doyle is arrested and Amanda is restored to Helene. The decision breaks Patrick and Angie's relationship, and she leaves him. Later Patrick visits the McCready home and finds Helene preparing to go out, casually leaving Amanda in his care and even misstating the name of her favorite doll. He stays to babysit. Amanda is legally home, but the closing scene makes clear that the moral cost Patrick feared has not vanished and that the better household he dismantled may indeed have offered the child greater care.
recaps.in_short: Boston investigators Patrick Kenzie and Angie Gennaro are hired to find four-year-old Amanda McCready, who disappeared while her neglectful mother Helene was at a bar. The search uncovers drug money stolen by Helene and an associate, drawing police and violent criminals into an apparent exchange in which Amanda is believed dead. Later inconsistencies expose a staged element to the case. Amanda is alive and living happily with retired police captain Jack Doyle, the final beneficiary of a conspiracy involving her uncle Lionel and people inside the investigation who intended to remove her from Helene. Angie wants to leave the child in the safer home; Patrick insists that kidnapping cannot be legitimized by their private judgment and calls the police. Amanda returns to Helene, Doyle is arrested, and Angie leaves Patrick over his choice. In the final scene Helene goes on a date and leaves Patrick to babysit, confirming the neglect that made his legally correct decision morally painful.

recaps.text: Before this case, Patrick Kenzie and Angela Gennaro have built a private-investigation partnership in Dorchester, the Boston neighborhood that formed them both. Their work depends on local knowledge, a willingness to enter violent situations, and help from Patrick's heavily armed friend Bubba Rogowski. Patrick and Angie also share an intimate, complicated bond. Earlier investigations have shown that they trust each other's skill while sometimes reaching different moral conclusions about what justice demands.

Four-year-old Amanda McCready disappears from a Dorchester apartment after her mother Helene leaves her alone and goes to a bar. Amanda's aunt and uncle, Beatrice and Lionel, hire Patrick Kenzie and Angie Gennaro because neighborhood residents who distrust police may speak to local private investigators. The official case is led by detectives Remy Broussard and Nick Poole under Captain Jack Doyle, whose own daughter was once abducted and murdered. Patrick and Angie quickly find that Helene is an unreliable parent and witness, more responsive to publicity than to ordinary responsibility. The crowded apartment, conflicting family accounts, and absence of a simple forced entry suggest that Amanda's disappearance may be tied to people who know Helene rather than to an unknown predator.

The investigators learn that Helene and a criminal associate stole a large amount of money from drug dealer Cheese Olamon. Her attempt to conceal the theft provides both a motive for the kidnapping and a reason she has withheld information while her daughter is missing. Patrick and Angie move between police contacts, neighborhood informants, and Cheese's organization, with Bubba available when the danger exceeds normal investigative work. Cheese's threats make an exchange of money for Amanda appear possible, but the information reaching the investigators is manipulated and incomplete. The case increasingly looks like a collision between Helene's reckless choices and criminals willing to use a child as pressure.

A dangerous attempt is made to recover Amanda through the people connected to the stolen money. The confrontation erupts into violence, and evidence at the scene leads Patrick, Angie, and the police to believe that Amanda has fallen into deep water and died. Her body is not recovered, leaving grief without certainty. The result devastates Angie and Patrick, who review the decisions that brought armed adults and a small child to the same place. Cheese's criminal network explains much of the immediate danger, but it does not resolve every inconsistency about how Amanda was removed from her home, who controlled the supposed exchange, or why some details of the operation fit too neatly.

After Amanda's presumed death, another endangered-child case brings Patrick and Angie into contact with extreme abuse and reinforces the personal stakes of their work. Violence within that investigation leaves further deaths and raises questions about conduct inside the police effort. Patrick continues examining contradictions from Amanda's disappearance rather than accepting the official sequence. Statements, timing, and the behavior of people close to the case suggest that the drug-money explanation was used to conceal another plan. The possibility emerges that at least one trusted participant knew more about Amanda's fate than was disclosed and that the tragedy at the exchange may have been staged to end the search.

Patrick's questions expose involvement by people who had presented themselves as allies. Remy Broussard is tied to the deception, and the unraveling conspiracy brings more violence before he can fully answer for it. Lionel McCready also knew that Amanda's removal was not a conventional kidnapping by Cheese's organization. The plan combined the stolen-money crisis with a desire to take Amanda away from Helene's neglect, then used her apparent death to stop further searching. Patrick and Angie realize that Amanda may still be alive. Their focus shifts from punishing the drug criminals to tracing where the child was taken and determining who now has her.

Patrick and Angie find Amanda alive with Jack Doyle, living in a stable and affectionate home. The former captain and others involved in the abduction believed that removing her from Helene was a rescue that ordinary law would never accomplish. Angie agrees that the child's well-being should outweigh Helene's parental rights and urges Patrick to walk away. Patrick cannot accept secretly authorizing a kidnapping, even for a better outcome, and contacts the authorities. Doyle is arrested and Amanda is returned to her mother. Angie leaves Patrick because his decision has placed the child back in the neglect they witnessed. When Patrick later visits, Helene is preparing for a date and readily leaves Amanda with him, while referring to the girl's beloved doll by the wrong name. Patrick stays to babysit, confronting the painful result of a choice that upheld the law without ensuring Amanda a caring home.

characters.description: A former New York magazine writer who lost his job in the media downturn and moved with his wife back to his Missouri hometown, where he runs a bar with his twin sister. On the morning of his fifth wedding anniversary he comes home to find signs of a struggle and his wife gone. As the police and public scrutinize him, his evasions, awkward public manner, and buried secrets quickly make him the prime suspect in her disappearance.
characters.name: Nick Dunne

characters.description: Nick's beautiful, brilliant wife, a New Yorker and former quiz writer whose childhood was the basis for her parents' bestselling Amazing Amy children's books. Her side of the story is told through diary entries that trace the couple's romance, marriage, and slide into money troubles and unhappiness after the move to Missouri. She vanishes from their home on their anniversary, leaving behind unsettling clues and a portrait of a marriage far more troubled than it seemed.
characters.name: Amy Dunne

characters.description: Nick's twin sister and closest confidante, who co-owns the bar with him. Blunt, loyal, and clear-eyed, she is the one person Nick trusts completely, and she stands by him as suspicion mounts, even as his secrets test her faith in him.
characters.name: Margo Dunne

characters.description: The lead detective on the case of Amy's disappearance. Shrewd, patient, and observant, she conducts the investigation with a low-key persistence, noticing the details of the crime scene and Nick's behavior that do not add up and steadily building a case.
characters.name: Rhonda Boney

characters.description: A local police detective who works the investigation alongside Rhonda Boney. More openly skeptical of Nick than his partner, he presses the theory that the husband is responsible.
characters.name: James Gilpin

characters.description: Amy's father, one half of the couple who wrote the famous Amazing Amy books loosely inspired by their daughter. Warm and publicly composed, he and his wife come to town during the search and become a visible, emotional presence in the media coverage of Amy's disappearance.
characters.name: Rand Elliott

characters.description: Amy's mother and co-author of the Amazing Amy series. Devoted to her daughter and initially fond of Nick, she joins the search and watches the investigation with growing worry as questions about Nick multiply.
characters.name: Marybeth Elliott

characters.description: A wealthy former boyfriend from Amy's youth, described in her account as an intense, possessive figure who never fully let go of her. His name surfaces as part of Amy's past, a man whose long fixation on her makes him a lingering shadow over the story.
characters.name: Desi Collings

recaps.ending: The novel's turn is that Amy is not a victim but the architect of the whole affair. Furious at Nick's affair with a young student and at the ruin of the life she wanted, she faked her own disappearance and death, keeping a false diary and staging clues designed to send Nick to prison for murdering her, then went into hiding to watch him fall. Her scheme unravels when other people at her hideout rob her of her cash. Desperate, she contacts Desi Collings, an obsessive wealthy ex-boyfriend, who installs her at his lakeside house under his control. To escape and to rewrite herself as a sympathetic survivor, Amy seduces Desi, kills him by cutting his throat, and returns home covered in his blood, claiming he had kidnapped and assaulted her. The story makes her a national heroine, and the police case against Nick collapses. Nick knows the truth but cannot prove it, and the public adoration shields her. When he prepares to leave her, Amy reveals she is pregnant, having used sperm he had once banked. Unwilling to abandon his child to her, and bound to her by their mutual knowledge, Nick remains, and the book closes on the two of them locked together in a marriage built on fear and performance.
recaps.in_short: On his fifth wedding anniversary, Nick Dunne finds his wife Amy missing from their Missouri home amid signs of a struggle. Told in alternating voices, Nick's present-day account and Amy's diary, the story makes Nick look increasingly guilty as his lies and an affair come to light. Halfway through, the truth flips: Amy is alive and has meticulously staged her own disappearance, faking a diary and planting evidence to frame Nick for her murder as revenge for his infidelity and the collapse of their marriage. Her plan goes awry when she is robbed while hiding out and turns for help to Desi Collings, a rich, controlling old boyfriend. Broke and cornered, she reinvents her story: she murders Desi, then returns home drenched in his blood claiming he abducted and raped her. The public sympathy this wins her makes it impossible for Nick to expose her. She reveals she has made herself pregnant with his stored sperm, and Nick, trapped by the threat to the child and by her willingness to destroy him, stays in the marriage.

recaps.text: Nick Dunne and his wife Amy are former New York writers who lost their media jobs and relocated to Nick's small Missouri hometown, where he now runs a bar with his twin sister. Their marriage, once glamorous, has grown strained under money worries and distance. On the morning of their fifth wedding anniversary, Nick returns home to find the living room disturbed and Amy gone. The police open a missing-person investigation that soon centers on Nick himself, whose flat affect and inconsistencies draw suspicion. The narrative alternates between Nick's account of the search and Amy's diary, which recounts how they met and married and how their relationship changed after the move, setting up a portrait of a troubled marriage and a disappearance that everyone is trying to explain.

characters.description: A former military policeman riding a late-night New York subway train. His counterterrorism experience leads him to study an unidentified passenger as a possible immediate threat, although he has not confirmed what she intends to do.
characters.name: Jack Reacher

characters.description: An unidentified woman passenger dressed in black on a late-night New York subway train. Her appearance and behavior lead Jack Reacher to consider her a possible immediate threat, although her identity and intentions remain unknown.
characters.name: Unnamed woman passenger

characters.description: Jacob Mark's missing adopted sister. Before disappearing, she was investigating a possible connection between John Sansom and Svetlana Hoth.
characters.name: Susan Mark

characters.description: An NYPD detective who receives Jacob Mark's report that Peter Molina may be missing. She is willing to examine new developments while leaving the already closed Susan Mark case officially undisturbed, pending stronger evidence.
characters.name: Theresa Lee

characters.description: An NYPD detective, Susan Mark's adopted brother, and Peter Molina's uncle. He reports Peter missing after the young man fails to attend football practice, and he supplies family details that may help explain the disappearance.
characters.name: Jacob Mark

characters.description: Susan Mark's son and a USC football player. He misses practice after leaving his coach a message that he is with a woman and may give up football. The message provides a possible explanation for his absence, but his safety has not been established.
characters.name: Peter Molina

characters.description: A politically connected man whose past may bear on Susan Mark's disappearance and her inquiry into Svetlana Hoth's account.
characters.name: John Sansom

characters.description: A wealthy, London-based Ukrainian widow who presents herself as Svetlana Hoth's daughter. She says Susan Mark became her telephone friend and had agreed to help identify an American soldier from Svetlana's past.
characters.name: Lila Hoth

characters.description: A Ukrainian-speaking former Red Army political commissar, introduced as Lila Hoth's mother. Lila claims that Svetlana knew an American soldier called John in Berlin in 1983, creating a possible link to Susan Mark's inquiry.
characters.name: Svetlana Hoth

characters.description: A former member of Lila Hoth's late husband's team who remains in her service. Lila identifies him as the man watching Reacher at Penn Station and says he was meant to make contact, although Reacher encountered him as a covert watcher.
characters.name: Leonid

characters.description: A man who warns Jack Reacher to abandon the protected military inquiry and says that pursuing the secret could provoke a lethal response from powerful officials.
characters.name: Springfield

characters.description: A Soviet sniper and Svetlana Hoth's husband in Lila's account of a 1983 operation in the Korengal Valley. Lila says American soldiers seized his specialized rifle and left him and his spotter exposed to capture.
characters.name: Grigori Hoth

characters.description: Theresa Lee's NYPD partner, who is reported to be under arrest while she and Reacher are fugitives. His predicament helps drive Lee's decision to surrender, stand beside him, and address the crisis through official channels.
characters.name: Docherty

characters.description: The delivery name used by Springfield when he sends a bag to Theresa Lee's precinct. The newly established identity explains who arranged the delivery, and Lee recognizes that the equipment inside is intended for Reacher.
characters.name: Browning

recaps.ending: Reacher draws seven Hoth operatives into an NYPD counterterrorism arrest at Union Square, escapes the federal agents waiting there, and enters the cell's 58th Street base alone. He kills the remaining male operatives, including a concealed twentieth man identified too late in the immigration count. After Lila Hoth and Svetlana Hoth disarm him, he uses a knife hidden against his back and kills them both, sustaining a serious abdominal wound. Theresa Lee and Springfield find him unconscious and take him to Bellevue Hospital. The Department of Defense assumes control of the nine bodies and prevents further consequences for Reacher. He concludes that Susan Mark threw her phone and the real memory stick from her car during an I-95 traffic jam after receiving evidence of Peter Molina's death. Searchers recover both items, but the stick is crushed beyond use, so the photograph of Sansom and Springfield cannot be exposed from it. Peter is treated as murdered, Susan's final fate remains unstated, and Reacher leaves New York. Lee survives and returns to police work, while Sansom's immediate political danger is contained.
recaps.in_short: Jack Reacher notices a distressed woman on a nearly empty New York subway train and becomes caught in the struggle over a missing memory stick. Susan Mark, a Pentagon employee, copied and erased an archive file containing a photograph of John Sansom and Springfield at a politically damaging 1983 meeting in Afghanistan. Lila Hoth and Svetlana Hoth target Susan through her son, Peter Molina, while federal personnel pursue Reacher and suppress the secret. Reacher works with NYPD detectives Theresa Lee and Jacob Mark, divides the Hoth cell with a staged exchange, and attacks its remaining members. He kills Lila, Svetlana, and the last operatives, but suffers a serious wound. Lee and Springfield get him to Bellevue Hospital. Reacher then identifies where Susan discarded the stick. It is recovered crushed and unreadable, leaving the photograph unusable. Peter was apparently murdered, Susan's ultimate fate is not established, and Reacher leaves New York.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Reacher is a former military policeman who travels independently and relies on his investigative and combat experience.

Reacher boards a nearly empty uptown subway train in New York at about two in the morning. He notices a woman dressed in black and tests her behavior against warning signs he learned during counterterrorism work. The hour and sparse passenger count make an attack seem strategically unlikely, but her oversized jacket is out of place in the September heat, and her visible strain, fixed gaze, repeated lip movements, and guarded messenger bag deepen his concern. He cannot determine whether the bag contains a weapon, yet its weight and the position of her hands suggest she may be controlling something concealed inside. Reacher considers warning the other passengers or clearing the car as the train continues through Manhattan. He decides that confusion, limited shared language, and the danger of provoking her make either choice unsafe. When he and the woman finally make eye contact, her response convinces him that she understands he is watching her. By the end of the chapter, he still has no confirmation that she is a bomber, but he believes the threat may be immediate.

Reacher's search leads him to the missing Susan Mark and to several groups seeking a memory stick she carried. Her brother, NYPD detective Jacob Mark, also reports that her son Peter Molina has disappeared. Detective Theresa Lee keeps Susan's case closed but follows the new concerns. Lila Hoth first claims that Susan was helping her mother, Svetlana Hoth, identify an American soldier from Berlin. She later replaces that story with an account of a 1983 operation in the Korengal Valley, where Americans took Soviet sniper Grigori Hoth's rifle. Lila believes John Sansom led that mission and wants the information Susan found. Sansom confirms privately that his team took the rifle, but says it released Grigori and his spotter. Reacher does not trust Lila's motives and refuses to surrender Susan's material. Four of Lila's men are then found dead, and Lila and Svetlana disappear from hotel records as if they were never guests. Reacher also recognizes Sansom's chief of staff as a passenger who had been near Susan on the subway. Federal agents seize Reacher, demand the real memory stick and Lila's location, and hold him in an unofficial cell when he refuses to cooperate.

Reacher wakes in a covert holding site with Theresa Lee and Jacob Mark confined nearby. He overpowers the interrogators and escapes, and all three later become fugitives under a false public account that they shot federal agents. Lila claims to be holding Peter Molina, while Reacher searches for her base near the Four Seasons and fights off Leonid and another operative. Lee eventually learns that her partner, Docherty, is apparently under arrest. She and Mark surrender so that Lee can support Docherty and Mark can seek an official search for Peter. Springfield then explains why Susan was targeted: as a Pentagon systems administrator, she copied a Delta archive file to a memory stick and deleted the original. The Hoths used Peter as leverage. A recording sent by Lila appears to show Lila and Svetlana torturing a Kabul taxi driver and then Peter, leaving Peter apparently dead. Reacher narrows the likely Hoth location to a neglected building near 58th Street. He tells Springfield that he can lead Sansom's side close to the real stick, but demands protection and help for Lee, Mark, Docherty, and Molina. Sansom meets him, although Reacher continues to withhold both the stick's location and the secret contained in the file.

Sansom and Springfield reveal that the missing file contains a photograph of them meeting the future al-Qaeda leader in Afghanistan in 1983. Its release would damage Sansom politically and embarrass the United States. Reacher decides to dismantle the Hoth cell. With equipment supplied through Springfield and information passed through Theresa Lee, he arranges a false sale of the memory-stick location. Seven operatives arrive at Union Square and are arrested by Lee's counterterrorism unit. Reacher evades Department of Defense agents, identifies the Hoths' hotel rooms, and attacks the remaining group at its 58th Street base. He kills the male operatives he encounters and reaches Lila and Svetlana. Lee warns him that the immigration count missed a concealed twentieth man, whom Reacher shoots with his last submachine-gun round. Lila and Svetlana disarm him and prepare to kill him, but he uses a knife taped to his back. He kills both women and is badly wounded. Lee and Springfield take him to Bellevue, and the Department of Defense suppresses the aftermath. Reacher deduces that Susan discarded her phone and the stick during an I-95 traffic jam after receiving proof of Peter's death. The recovered stick is crushed and unreadable. Susan's ultimate fate remains unstated, and Reacher leaves New York.

characters.description: The willful, green-eyed eldest daughter of the O'Hara family of Tara, a cotton plantation in north Georgia, on the eve of the Civil War. Sixteen, beautiful, and accustomed to being the belle of every gathering, she is far more practical, sharp, and headstrong than the demure Southern ladyhood her mother has tried to instill in her. She is infatuated with the neighboring planter Ashley Wilkes and cannot accept that he means to marry his gentle cousin Melanie. Vain and self-centered but fiercely determined, Scarlett pursues what she wants with little patience for convention.
characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara

characters.description: A young gentleman of the neighboring Twelve Oaks plantation, admired for his grace, his learning, and his dreamy, cultured manner. Scarlett has loved him for years and is dismayed by the news that he is to marry his quiet cousin Melanie Hamilton. Thoughtful and honorable, Ashley belongs to an old, genteel way of Southern life and seems poorly suited to the hardships the coming war will bring.
characters.name: Ashley Wilkes

characters.description: A dark, handsome, and notorious guest at the Twelve Oaks barbecue, received coldly by respectable society because he was expelled from West Point and cast off by his Charleston family. Cynical, blunt, and amused by the airs of the planter class, he speaks openly about the folly of secession while other men cheer for war. He happens to overhear Scarlett's private declaration of love to Ashley, and from that moment takes a knowing, mocking interest in her.
characters.name: Rhett Butler

characters.description: A plain, soft-spoken young woman from Atlanta, cousin and betrothed of Ashley Wilkes. Gentle, generous, and unfailingly kind, she thinks the best of everyone, including Scarlett, who privately resents her. Beneath her frail, retiring manner lies a quiet and unshakable strength and loyalty.
characters.name: Melanie Hamilton

characters.description: Scarlett's father, a hot-tempered, big-hearted Irish immigrant who won Tara at cards and built it into a thriving cotton plantation. Loud, hard-riding, and devoted to his land and his family, he adores his eldest daughter and is one of the few people who cannot refuse her.
characters.name: Gerald O'Hara

characters.description: Scarlett's mother, the serene and dignified mistress of Tara. Of aristocratic coastal stock, she runs the plantation household with tireless grace and piety, and embodies the gracious ladyhood she hopes Scarlett will one day inherit.
characters.name: Ellen O'Hara

characters.description: The formidable house servant who nursed Scarlett's mother and then Scarlett herself, and who rules the domestic life of Tara. Devoted, shrewd, and outspoken, she is forever trying to school the headstrong Scarlett in proper behavior.
characters.name: Mammy

characters.description: Melanie's shy, earnest younger brother. Smitten with Scarlett, he is easily won when she encourages him out of spite over Ashley, and the two are hastily married as the war begins.
characters.name: Charles Hamilton

characters.description: The fluttery, easily flustered elderly aunt of Charles and Melanie Hamilton, with whom the young Hamilton women keep house in Atlanta. Timid and prone to fainting spells, she is fond of gossip and comfort.
characters.name: Aunt Pittypat Hamilton

characters.description: A mild, fussy, middle-aged merchant and cautious suitor of Scarlett's younger sister Suellen. Old-fashioned in manner, he runs a store and nurses quiet ambitions to expand his trade.
characters.name: Frank Kennedy

characters.description: Scarlett's next younger sister, discontented and self-pitying, quick to complain and to envy. She regards Frank Kennedy as her beau and expects one day to marry him.
characters.name: Suellen O'Hara

recaps.ending: By the end, Scarlett has survived war, poverty, and three marriages and rebuilt her fortune, but her personal life collapses. Her marriage to Rhett Butler, long poisoned by her clinging to a romantic ideal of Ashley Wilkes, holds together mostly through their shared love for their daughter, Bonnie Blue. Bonnie's death in a riding accident destroys that last bond. Soon after, the saintly Melanie dies following a dangerous pregnancy, and in losing her Scarlett finally recognizes two truths at once: that Ashley was never the man she imagined and cannot manage without Melanie, and that the person she has truly loved is Rhett. She turns to him only to find him emptied of feeling, no longer willing to keep fighting for a wife who never valued him; he leaves, telling her plainly that he no longer cares. Left alone in Atlanta, Scarlett refuses despair. She fixes her thoughts on Tara, the land that has always restored her, and resolves to return there and find some way to bring Rhett back, certain that tomorrow will give her another chance.
recaps.in_short: On the eve of the Civil War, willful Georgia belle Scarlett O'Hara loves the genteel Ashley Wilkes, but he marries his gentle cousin Melanie, and Scarlett weds another man out of spite. Widowed young, she waits out the war in Atlanta, crossing paths again and again with the cynical blockade-runner Rhett Butler. When the city falls, she escapes the flames, delivers Melanie's baby, and returns to find her family's plantation, Tara, ruined and her mother dead. Vowing never to be hungry again, she claws her way back to wealth through two more marriages and hard, scandalous business dealing, at last marrying Rhett. Their union is stormy, held together mainly by their doted-on daughter, Bonnie. When Bonnie dies and then Melanie too, Scarlett finally sees that she has loved Rhett all along, but he has been worn past caring and leaves her. Undefeated, she turns back toward Tara to plan how to win him again.

recaps.text: In the spring of 1861, on the O'Hara cotton plantation of Tara in north Georgia, sixteen-year-old Scarlett O'Hara learns that the young planter she loves, Ashley Wilkes, is to marry his gentle cousin Melanie Hamilton. At a lavish barbecue at the Wilkes estate of Twelve Oaks, Scarlett corners Ashley and confesses her feelings, but he will not break with Melanie. Her furious outburst is overheard by Rhett Butler, a worldly, disreputable outsider who is unmoved by the region's eager talk of war. As the men rush to enlist after the firing on Fort Sumter, a wounded and spiteful Scarlett impulsively accepts the proposal of Melanie's shy brother, Charles Hamilton, and marries him, more to wound Ashley than out of any affection.

Scarlett's marriage is brief: Charles dies of illness in camp soon after the war begins, leaving her a resentful teenage widow with an infant son and none of the freedom she craved. Chafing at mourning, she goes to Atlanta to stay with Melanie and the fluttery Aunt Pittypat. There the bustling wartime city suits her restless energy, though widowhood forbids the gaiety she loves. At a charity bazaar she scandalizes society by dancing with the blockade-runner Rhett Butler, who reappears in her life and takes open, teasing pleasure in her company, seeing through her pretenses as no one else does. As the Confederacy's early confidence gives way to hardship and lengthening casualty lists, Scarlett waits out the war among people whose values she does not share, still secretly fixed on the absent Ashley.

As the war turns disastrous, Atlanta is besieged and shelled. Scarlett, held there by a promise to care for the pregnant Melanie, helps deliver Melanie's baby with almost no aid as the city falls. Rhett spirits the little group out through the burning streets, then abandons Scarlett on the road to join the doomed army, and she drives a broken-down wagon home through a ravaged countryside. She reaches Tara to find her mother dead, her father's mind shattered by grief, and the plantation stripped and starving. Vowing that she will never be hungry again, Scarlett takes brutal command of the family's survival, even killing a marauding deserter who threatens the house. Through back-breaking labor and ruthless will she keeps Tara alive amid the wreckage of the defeated South.

In the poverty of Reconstruction, a heavy new tax threatens Tara. Determined to save it, Scarlett steals her sister Suellen's staid merchant beau, Frank Kennedy, and marries him for his money. She shocks Atlanta by running Frank's store and buying a sawmill, driving hard bargains and dealing openly with Yankees and profiteers to rebuild her fortune, while Rhett lends her money and needles her about her methods. Her father dies, and she grows harder and richer as respectable society turns against her. After Scarlett is attacked while traveling alone, Frank rides out with a night raid of vigilantes to answer the insult and is killed. Widowed again, Scarlett is soon courted by Rhett, who proposes, and, half in love and half for security, she accepts.

Scarlett and Rhett marry, and his wealth gives her every luxury, but she cannot let go of her old dream of Ashley, and their marriage becomes a battle of pride. Their spirited daughter, Bonnie Blue, is the one person Rhett loves without reserve. When Scarlett is found in an innocent but compromising embrace with Ashley, Melanie refuses to believe any wrong and stands by her. Then tragedy strikes: Bonnie is killed in a riding accident, and the loss shatters both parents and the last thing that bound them. Melanie dies after a failed pregnancy, and only as she loses her does Scarlett realize that her long devotion to Ashley was an illusion and that she truly loves Rhett. She understands too late. Worn out and disillusioned, Rhett leaves her, indifferent to her pleading. Alone, Scarlett resolves to go back to Tara to gather her strength and find a way to win him back, trusting that tomorrow is another day.

characters.description: An angel who has been stationed on Earth since the Garden of Eden, now living as the fussy, book-loving proprietor of a rare and antiquarian bookshop in London. Fond of good food, old books, and the comforts of human life, he has grown far too attached to the world to want it to end. Over the millennia he has developed an unlikely, careful friendship with his opposite number among the demons.
characters.name: Aziraphale

characters.description: A demon who was present as the serpent in Eden and has worked Earth ever since, presenting himself as a stylish, sunglasses-wearing operator with a beloved vintage Bentley. Less wicked than easily bored, he has come to enjoy the modern world and its pleasures, and has no real appetite for its destruction. He and the angel Aziraphale have quietly become friends across the divide between their sides.
characters.name: Crowley

characters.description: An imaginative, charismatic eleven-year-old boy growing up in the ordinary English village of Lower Tadfield, the ringleader of a small gang of local children. Unknown to the adults around him and even to himself, he is no ordinary child: through a mix-up at his birth he was raised in this quiet village rather than where the forces of Heaven and Hell intended, and enormous power sleeps in him.
characters.name: Adam Young

characters.description: A young woman who is a practicing witch and occultist, and the last descendant of a seventeenth-century prophetess. She has spent her life guided by an inherited book of eerily accurate predictions, and she comes to Lower Tadfield on its instructions, trying to work out how to head off the disaster the prophecies foretell.
characters.name: Anathema Device

characters.description: A mild, awkward young man and hopeless amateur with computers and machines, which tend to break in his presence. Looking for something more meaningful, he answers an odd recruiting notice and becomes a modern member of a nearly defunct witch-hunting order, a role that sends him toward Lower Tadfield.
characters.name: Newton Pulsifer

characters.description: The cantankerous, unwashed, and deeply paranoid leader of the Witchfinder Army, a centuries-old witch-hunting organization now reduced to almost nothing but himself. Gruff and suspicious of everyone, he keeps the order technically alive by padding its rolls and cadging funds, and takes on Newton Pulsifer as a new recruit.
characters.name: Sergeant Shadwell

characters.description: Shadwell's neighbor, a kindly middle-aged woman who works as a part-time medium and offers other discreet services. Warm-hearted and unbothered by Shadwell's grumbling, she takes an interest in the sour old witchfinder living down the hall.
characters.name: Madame Tracy

characters.description: A seventeenth-century English witch and prophetess whose book, The Nice and Accurate Prophecies of Agnes Nutter, Witch, is the only wholly correct book of predictions ever written. Long dead before the main events, she foresaw the future with uncanny, often maddeningly cryptic precision, and her descendants have puzzled over her prophecies ever since.
characters.name: Agnes Nutter

recaps.ending: Armageddon is averted not by Heaven or Hell but by the free will of a single ordinary child. As the End Times arrive, the Antichrist, Adam Young, comes fully into his powers, but rather than destroying the world he has grown up loving, he refuses the role written for him. Confronted with the machinery of the Apocalypse, Adam dismisses the Four Horsemen, faces down the arriving forces of Heaven and Hell, and rejects Satan himself, denying that the being is truly his father because his real father is the human man who raised him. By choosing humanity over destiny, Adam calls off the end of the world, and reality settles back into place. In the aftermath, Aziraphale and Crowley must answer to their furious superiors for having sided with the world instead of the war. Forewarned by a final prophecy of Agnes Nutter, they swap appearances, so that when Hell tries to execute Crowley and Heaven tries to punish Aziraphale, each survives the ordeal meant for the other, and their masters give up on them. Newton Pulsifer and Anathema Device are left together, having burned the last of Agnes's prophecies to live their own lives free of foreknowledge. Adam returns to being an ordinary boy in Lower Tadfield, and the two old friends from opposite sides sit down to enjoy the world they saved.
recaps.in_short: The angel Aziraphale and the demon Crowley have spent millennia on Earth and, having grown fond of the world and of each other, dread the coming Apocalypse. The Antichrist has been born, but through a mix-up at the hospital the diabolical baby is sent home with an ordinary English family instead of the intended one, and grows up as Adam Young, a normal boy in the sleepy village of Lower Tadfield, while Heaven and Hell fuss over the wrong child. As Adam turns eleven and Armageddon approaches, his latent powers begin to wake, reshaping the world around him according to his boyish whims. Aziraphale and Crowley scramble to prevent the end of the world, aided and hindered by the witch Anathema Device, guided by her ancestor Agnes Nutter's uncannily accurate prophecies, and the hapless witchfinders Newton Pulsifer and Sergeant Shadwell. The Four Horsemen gather and the forces of Heaven and Hell mass for the final battle. In the end, Adam refuses the destiny chosen for him, rejecting his role as Antichrist and using his power to send the Horsemen away and defy his infernal father, stopping Armageddon by human choice. The world is saved, and Aziraphale and Crowley cleverly evade punishment from their respective sides.

recaps.text: The end of the world is scheduled, and neither the angel Aziraphale nor the demon Crowley wants it to happen. After thousands of years stationed on Earth, the two have come to love human life and, quietly, each other's company, and they would rather the world went on. The trouble is that the Antichrist has been born and is meant to be delivered to a prominent family so that he can grow up to trigger the Apocalypse. But a mix-up at the hospital sends the wrong baby home, and the true Antichrist is raised as Adam Young, an ordinary, imaginative boy in the tranquil English village of Lower Tadfield, while Heaven and Hell keep their eyes on the wrong child entirely. As Adam grows toward his eleventh birthday and the appointed day draws near, a sprawling cast is drawn toward Lower Tadfield, including a witch guided by a book of unnervingly accurate old prophecies and a pair of bumbling witch-hunters, all of them caught up, knowingly or not, in the countdown to Armageddon.

characters.description: Niece of King Randa of the Middluns and, since she was eight years old, the instrument of his anger. Her Grace appears to be killing: she is faster, stronger and deadlier than anyone alive, and Randa sends her to break fingers and frighten lords into paying what he demands. She loathes the work, and has built a secret answer to it in the Council, a small network that rides across the seven kingdoms undoing the cruelties of its kings. Blunt, impatient with court manners, and convinced she is a danger to everyone near her, she has decided she will never marry and never bear children.
characters.name: Katsa

characters.description: The seventh and youngest son of King Ror of Lienid, who arrives at Randa's court searching for his kidnapped grandfather. He wears the heavy gold rings and arm bands of a Lienid prince, and his Graced eyes are one gold and one silver. He is taken everywhere for a fighter, the only person who has ever come close to matching Katsa in a bout, and he is easy company where she is prickly, cheerfully curious about her and unafraid of what she can do.
characters.name: Po

characters.description: Captain of King Randa's guard and the man who gathers his intelligence, a steady, greying soldier who rides with Katsa on the Council's missions. He is one of its founding members and has a family in the city.
characters.name: Oll

characters.description: A young Middluns lord and one of the Council's founding members, who rides at Katsa's side on its missions. He is comfortable with Randa's court in a way Katsa is not, protective of her to the point of irritation, and hopes to marry her.
characters.name: Giddon

characters.description: King Randa's son and heir and Katsa's closest friend in the castle. He would far rather work with herbs and medicines than learn to rule, and his experiments occasionally leave his hair dyed blue. He hides the people the Council rescues in his workrooms and keeps its secrets from his father.
characters.name: Raffin

characters.description: Raffin's assistant in the medicine rooms and his constant companion, quiet and capable, trusted with everything the Council does.
characters.name: Bann

characters.description: King of the Middluns and Katsa's uncle, a large, loud man who has used his Graced niece as a public threat since she was a child. He is not the worst of the seven kings, but he cannot imagine being refused, and he keeps Katsa close because her reputation does his work for him.
characters.name: Randa

characters.description: A servant of Randa's court who has looked after Katsa since she was a small child. She is one of the very few people in the castle who is not frightened of her, and she says what she thinks about Katsa's clothes, her manners and her refusal to marry.
characters.name: Helda

characters.description: An elderly Lienid nobleman, grandfather of the Lienid royal children, taken from his home and held half-starved in a foreign dungeon. Nobody can work out why anyone would want an old man who holds no power and knows no secrets, which is exactly what makes his kidnapping worth investigating.
characters.name: Prince Tealiff

characters.description: King of Sunder, in whose dungeons the kidnapped Lienid grandfather is being kept. He deals in goods and information and asks few questions about the origin of either, and he keeps a Graced mind reader at his court.
characters.name: Murgon

characters.description: King of Monsea, a kingdom shut away behind mountains, and the one ruler in the seven kingdoms with a reputation for pure kindness: he takes in the sick, shelters orphaned animals and children, and is loved by his people. He wears a patch over one eye. As the Council traces the kidnapping, that reputation turns out to be the most dangerous thing about him, because his Grace works through his voice: what he says, people believe, and they forget having been made to believe it.
characters.name: Leck

characters.description: Queen of Monsea, born a Lienid princess and sister to King Ror, married to Leck and rarely seen outside Monsea since. She is the mother of the kingdom's only child heir, and her Lienid family has had almost no word from her in years.
characters.name: Ashen

characters.description: The ten-year-old heir to Monsea, half Lienid, small and half-starved when she is found hiding in the forest with her mother's blood on her. She has been raised inside her father's court and has learned to keep very still and say very little; underneath she is stubborn, sharply observant and far tougher than her size suggests, and she can hold a knife.
characters.name: Bitterblue

characters.description: King of Lienid, Po's father, a decisive ruler with the family's gold-and-jewel style and a good deal of his youngest son's charm. He commands a fleet and is willing to use it, and he is Queen Ashen's brother.
characters.name: Ror

recaps.ending: Katsa reaches the Lienid court with Bitterblue and learns that Leck has told the seven kingdoms that Katsa murdered Queen Ashen and stole the child, and that he has called the kingdoms' rulers to Monsea to settle the matter. King Ror sails with them. Because Leck's Grace works through his voice, the only safe way to face him is to stop him speaking: Katsa gets into the gathering hall and kills him with a thrown dagger before his words can take hold of the room. With his death the fog lifts from Monsea, and the extent of what he did to his people and his animals begins to surface. Bitterblue, ten years old, is made queen, with Ror staying on to steady the kingdom until she can rule it herself. Katsa then crosses back over the mountains and finds Po alive at the lakeside hut, blinded by his injuries and hiding it, using his Grace to move through a world he can no longer see. She refuses to let him disappear, and he agrees to come back. They end the book together on Katsa's terms: no marriage, no promises to stay, and a plan to keep the Council running and to teach girls across the seven kingdoms how to fight.
recaps.in_short: In the seven kingdoms, a rare few are born Graced with an extreme skill, marked by two different-coloured eyes. Katsa, niece of King Randa of the Middluns, believes her Grace is killing, and has been used as her uncle's enforcer since childhood while secretly running the Council, which undoes the harm the seven kings do. Rescuing a kidnapped Lienid grandfather, she meets Po, a Lienid prince whose Grace is not fighting but perception - he senses the world around him and every thought that concerns him. Together they work out that the kidnapping leads to King Leck of Monsea, whose famous kindness is a lie held up by a Grace that makes people believe whatever he says. In Monsea they find Leck's wife murdered and his daughter Bitterblue in flight. Po holds Leck off while Katsa takes the child over the winter mountains, discovering on the way that her Grace was never killing but survival. Katsa returns to kill Leck before he can speak, Bitterblue is crowned queen at ten, and Katsa goes back for Po, who has been blinded but can still see through his Grace.

recaps.text: In the seven kingdoms a very small number of people are born Graced, marked by two different-coloured eyes and possessed of one skill carried to an impossible extreme. Katsa, niece of King Randa of the Middluns, is believed to be Graced with killing; she has been her uncle's enforcer since she was eight, sent to maim and frighten people who displease him, and she hates it. In secret she runs the Council with Prince Raffin, the guard captain Oll and Lord Giddon: a small network that quietly undoes the cruelties of the seven kings. The book opens with a Council mission into King Murgon's dungeons in Sunder to free an elderly Lienid nobleman, Prince Tealiff, who has been kidnapped for no reason anyone can see. On her way out Katsa is intercepted in the dark by a Graced fighter who is nearly her equal; she knocks him unconscious rather than kill him, and the Council carries Tealiff back to the Middluns to hide him in Raffin's workrooms while they try to work out who took him and why.

The man from Murgon's courtyard turns up at Randa's court: he is Po, youngest son of King Ror of Lienid and Tealiff's grandson, searching for the old man himself. Recognising each other, they come to an understanding, and Po is brought into the Council's confidence and reunited with his grandfather. The two of them begin sparring daily, the first time in Katsa's life she has fought anyone she cannot easily beat, and the first time she has been treated as a person rather than a weapon. Together the Council works the kidnapping backwards: none of the seven kingdoms gains anything by holding a harmless old man, and Murgon was clearly storing him for somebody else. Tealiff, when he recovers enough to speak, cannot explain it either. Meanwhile Randa continues to hand Katsa assignments, and her willingness to carry them out is wearing thin.

Randa orders Katsa to punish a lord who has crossed him, and she refuses. Rather than run, she walks into his great hall and makes it plain that he has no way to compel her and no way to stop her leaving, and the king, who has spent his life pointing her at other people, backs down in front of his own court. Katsa gives up her place in the Middluns and sets out with Po to find who took his grandfather, leaving the Council in Raffin, Oll and Giddon's hands. The trail points east and the suspicion narrows to Monsea, the mountain-ringed kingdom whose king, Leck, is famous throughout the seven kingdoms for his gentleness - he takes in the sick and the orphaned, and he married Tealiff's daughter, the Lienid princess Ashen. Nothing about that reputation should make him a kidnapper, which is precisely what starts to trouble them.

Travelling alone together, Katsa learns that Po has been lying to the world about his Grace. He is not Graced with fighting: he perceives the physical world around him without needing to see it, and he senses the thoughts of anyone thinking about him. His family hid it when he was a child because a king who knew would either use him or kill him, and only his mother and grandfather share the secret. Katsa is furious at having been read, then accepts it, and the two become lovers on the road, on the understanding that Katsa will not marry anyone. With Po's Grace to test their reasoning, they arrive at an answer to the kidnapping: Leck's reputation for kindness is not a fact but a story he is able to make people believe, because his Grace works through his voice. It explains why nobody in Monsea questions the disappearances at his court, why Ashen has been out of contact for years, and why Tealiff, who may have begun to suspect something, had to be taken quietly.

Knowing that hearing Leck speak is enough to lose your own mind to him, Katsa and Po go into Monsea anyway. In the forest they find Queen Ashen dead, killed while getting her daughter away from the castle, and the ten-year-old heir Bitterblue hiding nearby, hunted by her father's men. Leck's story is already running ahead of them: the kingdom is being told that Katsa murdered the queen and stole the child. When Leck himself comes close, Po sends Katsa away with Bitterblue and stays behind to hold him off, knowing his own Grace gives him a chance nobody else has of resisting a voice he cannot help hearing. Katsa and the child flee south with Leck's riders behind them and no way of knowing whether Po survived.

With every road watched, Katsa takes Bitterblue over the mountains in the depth of winter - a crossing nobody attempts in that season - hunting and building fires and carrying the child through snow for weeks. Somewhere in that ordeal Katsa finally understands what her Grace actually is. She was never Graced with killing: she is Graced with survival, which is why she cannot be beaten, cannot be starved, cannot freeze, and learns any skill that keeps her alive almost instantly. The distinction changes what she believes about herself, because the thing Randa built his threats on was a misunderstanding of a girl who had simply never been allowed to be anything else. The two of them come down out of the mountains to the coast of Sunder and take ship for Lienid, where Bitterblue can be hidden among Po's family while Katsa works out what to do about Leck.

In Lienid, Katsa learns that Leck has summoned the rulers of the seven kingdoms to Monsea to hear his account of the murdered queen and the stolen child, and that his voice in that room would end any hope of the truth. King Ror sails with them. Katsa gets into the hall and kills Leck with a thrown dagger before he can talk his way into anyone's head, and Monsea comes out of the fog he kept it in, uncovering the cruelties he committed on his own people and animals for thirty-five years. Bitterblue is crowned queen at ten, with Ror remaining to steady the kingdom for her. Katsa then recrosses the mountains and finds Po alive at a lakeside hut: he survived Leck, but his injuries left him blind, and he has been hiding it and living through his Grace alone. She refuses to leave him there. They return together, and Katsa keeps the terms she has always kept - no marriage, no promise to stay in one place - and sets out to keep the Council alive and to teach girls across the seven kingdoms to fight.

characters.description: Chicago's professional wizard, now working alongside the Knight of the Cross Michael Carpenter to deal with a wave of ghosts and spirits that have turned violent. More established than in his first cases but no less broke or reckless, Harry is stalked by an old debt and by his own habit of taking on more than he can safely carry. His fierce loyalty to the people he loves is about to be turned into a weapon against him, and his temper about to cost him more than he imagines.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: A Knight of the Cross, one of a tiny number of mortals chosen to wield a holy sword against the worst evils in the world. Michael carries Amoracchius, a blade said to hold one of the nails of the Crucifixion, and fights with a faith as solid as his broad shoulders. A devout Catholic and a devoted husband and father, he is Harry's opposite in temper - patient, humble, and certain where Harry is cynical and profane - and he becomes Harry's steadfast partner in hunting the tormented spirits plaguing the city. He disapproves of Harry's rough edges but trusts his heart.
characters.name: Michael Carpenter

characters.description: Michael's wife: heavily pregnant, fiercely devoted to her large family, and openly hostile to Harry, whom she blames for drawing her husband into danger. Strong-willed and unafraid to say exactly what she thinks, Charity guards her home and children with everything she has, which makes her and her unborn child a target when Harry's enemies choose to strike at those he cares for.
characters.name: Charity Carpenter

characters.description: Harry's faerie godmother, a Sidhe noblewoman of the Winter Court, beautiful and utterly without human mercy. Long ago Harry bargained away a claim on himself to her, and now the Leanansidhe means to collect - to take him into Faerie and remake him as her own creature. She pursues him through the book, an elegant, patient predator who offers help laced with traps, bound by faerie rules that Harry must exploit to keep his freedom.
characters.name: The Leanansidhe

characters.description: The reporter who chases the supernatural, and Harry's girlfriend, still pressing for the truth of his world and still refusing to be protected from it. Susan's closeness to Harry makes her a mark for the enemies circling him, and her determination to be part of his life draws her toward the vampires' orbit and a danger far greater than any story.
characters.name: Susan Rodriguez

characters.description: The Red Court vampire Harry humiliated during his first case, returned far more powerful and poised. Now elevated among her kind and hosting a grand masquerade ball to mark her rise, Bianca has spent the years plotting a patient, elaborate revenge. Beneath the gracious hostess is a cold, vindictive predator who has arranged events across the city to draw Harry into a trap of her making.
characters.name: Bianca

characters.description: A malevolent spirit tormenting first the ghosts and then the living of Chicago, growing stronger with each victim. It stalks people through their dreams, poisoning and draining them, and singles out those closest to Harry. It proves to be the risen ghost of Kravos, a murderous sorcerer Harry and Michael destroyed not long before; freed and warped in death, and set loose by others for their own ends, it has become one of the deadliest things Harry has faced.
characters.name: The Nightmare

characters.description: A languid, beautiful young man who appears at Bianca's masquerade and, to Harry's surprise, quietly takes his side. Thomas is a vampire of the White Court, whose kind feed on human emotion and desire rather than blood and who wear their humanity far more convincingly than the Red Court. Vain, charming, and hard to read, he has reasons of his own for helping Harry survive the ball, and an interest in him that he does not explain.
characters.name: Thomas Raith

characters.description: A lovely, fragile young woman who attends the masquerade at Thomas's side, bound to him as his lover and the source he feeds upon. Devoted to Thomas despite what he is, Justine moves through the vampires' world in constant quiet danger, and her bond with him hints that this White Court vampire is not quite as heartless as his kind are meant to be.
characters.name: Justine

characters.description: An ancient and terrifying vampire of the Black Court - the classic bloodsucking undead of legend, rotted and inhumanly strong. Mavra is a sorceress as well as a monster, able to work magic few of her kind command, and she attends Bianca's gathering as a guest of appalling power. Cold, patient, and centuries old, she marks Harry as an enemy worth remembering.
characters.name: Mavra

recaps.ending: Harry destroys the Nightmare - the ghost of the sorcerer Kravos - ending the plague of tormented spirits, and with Michael he saves Charity Carpenter and her newborn son. But the cost of the case is enormous. At Bianca's masquerade, Susan Rodriguez was bitten and infected with the Red Court's curse; caught between human and vampire and terrified of what she might do to the people around her, she leaves Chicago, and Harry, behind. Harry's furious massacre of Bianca and her court, in violation of the guest-truce, has dragged the entire White Council into open war with the Red Court - a war they hold him responsible for starting, and one that will shadow him for years. Thomas Raith, the White Court vampire who unexpectedly helped him, slips away with his secrets and his unexplained interest in Harry intact. Michael Carpenter is now Harry's closest and most trusted ally. Harry ends victorious over the immediate evil but heartbroken, isolated by loss, and freshly burdened with a war he never meant to start and a Council that trusts him even less than before.
recaps.in_short: Working alongside Michael Carpenter, a Knight of the Cross who wields a holy sword, Harry Dresden confronts a wave of ghosts driven violent across Chicago while dodging his faerie godmother, the Leanansidhe, who has come to claim an old debt. The disturbances are the work of the Nightmare, a dream-stalking spirit that proves to be the risen ghost of a sorcerer Harry helped destroy - and it has been set loose deliberately, striking at everyone Harry loves. Behind it all is his old enemy, the Red Court vampire Bianca, now risen in power and staging a grand masquerade as an elaborate revenge. Bianca captures Harry's girlfriend Susan to lure him in; at the ball Susan is bitten and cursed into a half-vampire state, and Harry, enraged, destroys Bianca and her court - an act that ignites open war between the White Council and the Red Court. Harry kills the Nightmare and saves the Carpenters' baby, but Susan, unable to trust herself, leaves him, and he is left blamed for a war.

recaps.text: Previously: Harry Dresden, Chicago's only professional wizard and a police consultant, has survived a rogue heart-ripping sorcerer and a tangle of warring werewolves. Along the way he rebuilt his uneasy partnership with Detective Karrin Murphy, gained loyal allies in Billy and the shapeshifting college pack called the Alphas, and stayed under the wary watch of the White Council of wizards. From his first case he carries a dangerous enemy: the Red Court vampire Bianca, whom he humiliated and who has been quietly climbing in power ever since. He is dating Susan Rodriguez, a fearless reporter who chases the supernatural stories he will not give her.

A year on from the werewolf killings, Harry has taken up an unlikely partner: Michael Carpenter, a Knight of the Cross who wields a holy sword against the darkness. Across Chicago the barrier between the living world and the spirit realm has grown thin, and ghosts are rising in torment and turning violent. Harry and Michael hunt these disturbances down one by one, but it becomes clear that something is deliberately stirring the dead into a frenzy. Meanwhile Harry is stalked by his own faerie godmother, the Leanansidhe, who has come to collect an old debt and carry him into Faerie, and he must dodge her elegant traps while the spirit crisis worsens.

The force behind the rising dead reveals itself as the Nightmare, a spirit that hunts people through their dreams, draining and torturing them and growing stronger with every victim. It targets those closest to Harry - striking at Michael's pregnant wife Charity and their unborn child, and at others in his circle - to wound him through the people he loves. Harry realizes the Nightmare is the risen ghost of Kravos, a sorcerer he and Michael had destroyed, and that someone freed and unleashed it on purpose. As he races to protect his friends and unmask whoever is directing the spirit, an engraved invitation arrives: the Red Court vampire Bianca, his old enemy, is hosting a grand masquerade ball.

The threads converge on Bianca. Recovered from the humiliation of their first encounter and risen high among the Red Court, she has orchestrated the whole crisis as an intricate revenge, and her ball is the trap at its heart. She seizes Susan to force Harry to attend. Bound by the customs of such a gathering and desperate to save Susan, Harry and Michael walk into a hall full of monsters: Red Court nobles, the ancient Black Court sorceress Mavra, and other horrors. There Harry gains one unexpected ally in Thomas Raith, a White Court vampire who takes his side for reasons of his own, while the ball tightens around them as a carefully sprung snare.

The masquerade turns to violence. The vampires spring their trap, and Susan is bitten and infected with the Red Court's curse - left half-turned, forced from then on to fight an endless thirst. Enraged past reason, Harry breaks the guest-truce and destroys Bianca and much of her court in a storm of fire, but the act carries a terrible price: it is a declaration of open war between the wizards' White Council and the Red Court, a war the Council will blame on him. With Thomas and Michael's help, Harry and the survivors escape the ruin of the ball.

Harry hunts down and destroys the Nightmare, the ghost of Kravos, ending the torment of the city's dead, and he and Michael save Charity and her newborn son. But the greater damage is done. Susan, now cursed and struggling to keep from fully becoming a vampire, cannot stay near the people she might harm and leaves Chicago and Harry behind. Harry's slaughter at Bianca's ball has dragged the entire White Council into a war with the Red Court that will hang over him for years. He ends the book victorious over the immediate threat but stripped of the woman he loves, blamed for a war, and bound more tightly than ever to Michael Carpenter, who has become his truest ally.

characters.description: An orphan being raised in the Kent marshes by his older sister and her husband Joe. Frightened and imaginative, he tells his own story from adulthood, beginning with a childhood encounter that tests his fear, pity, and conscience.
characters.name: Philip Pirrip

characters.description: A desperate escaped prisoner whom Pip meets in a churchyard. He threatens the boy into bringing food and a file, yet his hunger and exposure also awaken Pip's sympathy.
characters.name: The convict

characters.description: Pip's brother-in-law, a village blacksmith of great physical strength and exceptional gentleness. He treats Pip as a companion rather than a burden and quietly protects him from the severity of their home.
characters.name: Joe Gargery

characters.description: Pip's much older sister and guardian. Proud of having raised him, she maintains the household through anger, punishment, and constant reminders of his dependence.
characters.name: Mrs Joe Gargery

characters.description: Joe's pompous uncle, a grain merchant who claims credit for arranging Pip's first visit to Miss Havisham. He habitually treats Pip as ungrateful and inferior.
characters.name: Mr Pumblechook

characters.description: A kind, practical girl connected with Pip's village school. She helps Pip learn and later assists in the Gargery household, becoming a friend who sees his ambitions more clearly than he does.
characters.name: Biddy

characters.description: A wealthy recluse who receives Pip in a decaying mansion where the clocks have been stopped and the remains of her wedding day are preserved. Still dressed as a bride, she makes the bewildered boy play for her amusement.
characters.name: Miss Havisham

characters.description: A beautiful, proud girl raised in Miss Havisham's house. She openly mocks Pip's coarse hands and speech, making him painfully conscious of class and eager to become someone she might respect.
characters.name: Estella

characters.description: A formidable London lawyer whose abrupt manner and command of other people impress Pip. He arrives at the forge with news that an unnamed benefactor will finance Pip's transformation into a gentleman.
characters.name: Mr Jaggers

characters.description: A cheerful young Londoner who helps Pip settle into his new rooms and becomes his closest friend. Pip then recognizes him as the boy he once fought at Satis House.
characters.name: Herbert Pocket

characters.description: Jaggers's dry, methodical clerk. At the office he appears guarded and mechanical, but he takes a friendly interest in Pip and offers practical guidance about London life.
characters.name: John Wemmick

characters.description: A wealthy, sullen young man studying with the Pocket household. Proud of his social position and physically powerful, he treats those around him with contempt.
characters.name: Bentley Drummle

characters.description: A resentful journeyman at Joe's forge. He dislikes Pip, quarrels readily, and carries a grievance against anyone he thinks has been favored above him.
characters.name: Dolge Orlick

characters.description: Another transported criminal whose history is closely entangled with that of Pip's benefactor. His polished appearance once allowed him to present himself very differently from his rougher associate.
characters.name: Compeyson

recaps.ending: Pip and Herbert try to send Magwitch abroad, but the authorities intercept their boat. Compeyson dies in the struggle, Magwitch is captured, and the fortune intended for Pip is lost to the state. Before Magwitch dies, Pip comforts him and tells him that his lost daughter is alive and has become a beautiful woman. Pip then falls gravely ill and awakens to find Joe caring for him and paying his debts. Humbled, Pip returns home intending to marry Biddy, only to discover that she and Joe have just married each other. He accepts their happiness and later works abroad with Herbert, gradually repaying Joe. Years afterward, he meets a changed, widowed Estella in the ruins of Satis House. They leave together in friendship, and Pip sees no prospect of another separation.
recaps.in_short: Orphaned Pip helps a frightening escaped convict, then becomes ashamed of his humble life after meeting wealthy Miss Havisham and her proud ward Estella. When an anonymous benefactor pays for him to become a London gentleman, Pip assumes Miss Havisham intends him for Estella and grows distant from the faithful blacksmith Joe. His true patron is instead Abel Magwitch, the convict Pip aided as a child, who made a fortune after transportation. Pip overcomes his shock and risks himself to help Magwitch escape, but the attempt fails and Magwitch dies in custody after losing his fortune. Pip's debts and illness bring Joe back to care for him without resentment. Humbled, Pip learns that Joe has married Biddy, works with Herbert abroad, and rebuilds his life honestly. Much later he meets the widowed, chastened Estella at ruined Satis House, and they part no more.

recaps.text: Pip, an orphan living with his severe sister and her kind blacksmith husband Joe, meets an escaped convict in a marshland churchyard. Terrified by the man's threats, Pip steals food and a file for him, though compassion mixes with fear. Soldiers later ask Joe to repair handcuffs and take the household to watch the search. Two convicts are caught fighting. To protect Pip, the man Pip helped claims he stole the food himself. The incident ends without Pip's theft being exposed, but it leaves him with a lasting mixture of guilt and sympathy.

Pip is sent to entertain the rich, reclusive Miss Havisham at Satis House. He finds her still dressed for a wedding that never occurred, surrounded by the decaying remains of the interrupted celebration. Her ward Estella mocks Pip's speech, clothes, and working hands. Pip becomes infatuated with her and ashamed of the forge and of Joe, despite Joe's unfailing kindness. Miss Havisham encourages his emotional dependence on Estella but eventually arranges for Pip to be formally apprenticed to Joe. Pip tries to educate himself with Biddy's help, while the bitter forge worker Orlick becomes increasingly hostile. An attack leaves Mrs Joe badly injured, and Biddy comes to care for the household.

The lawyer Jaggers announces that Pip has great expectations from an anonymous benefactor and must move to London to be educated as a gentleman. Pip assumes Miss Havisham is preparing him to marry Estella. He leaves Joe and Biddy with growing condescension, though Joe asks for nothing from him. In London, Pip befriends Herbert Pocket, learns the story of Miss Havisham's abandonment before her wedding, and meets Jaggers's clerk Wemmick. He also joins a circle that includes the unpleasant Bentley Drummle. Pip acquires expensive habits and debts. When Joe visits, Pip is embarrassed by him, a response that exposes how far his expectations have separated him from the people who genuinely love him.

Pip returns home after Mrs Joe's death but does little to repair his relationships with Joe and Biddy. Estella comes to London and calmly warns Pip that she has been trained not to love, yet he persists in imagining a future with her. Pip secretly uses part of his allowance to help Herbert enter a business partnership. On his twenty-third birthday he still receives no name for his patron. The mystery ends when the convict from the marshes, now calling himself Abel Magwitch, appears at Pip's rooms. Having prospered after transportation, Magwitch has devoted his fortune to making Pip a gentleman in gratitude for the child's kindness. Pip is horrified to learn that his wealth has no connection to Miss Havisham and that Estella was never promised to him.

Because returning from transportation can cost Magwitch his life, Pip and Herbert hide him and plan an escape by river. Magwitch tells them about Compeyson, the polished criminal who exploited him and received a lighter sentence because he appeared respectable. Pip realizes Compeyson was also the man who abandoned Miss Havisham. Wemmick warns that Pip's rooms are being watched. Pip confronts Miss Havisham about the false hopes she encouraged; she agrees to finance Herbert's future and begins to recognize the harm she has done. Estella nevertheless marries the brutal Drummle. Miss Havisham's dress later catches fire, and Pip burns his hands while saving her, but she is badly injured.

Orlick lures Pip to an isolated building, admits his hatred and his attack on Mrs Joe, and prepares to kill him. Herbert and others arrive in time to rescue Pip. Pip then joins Herbert and Magwitch in the planned river escape, but a pursuing boat intercepts them. Magwitch and Compeyson struggle in the water; Compeyson drowns, while the injured Magwitch is captured. His property is forfeited, ending Pip's expectations. Pip stays beside him through trial and illness and, before Magwitch dies, tells him that the daughter he lost is alive and loved. Overwhelmed by debt and fever, Pip is nursed by Joe, who also settles his creditors. Pip returns home intending to ask Biddy to marry him but finds that she and Joe have married. He later works with Herbert abroad and becomes self-supporting. Years afterward, he meets the widowed Estella at the ruins of Satis House. Both have been changed by suffering, and they leave together with no expectation of another parting.
